findings.claim: `prefix` is newly passed into `trpcMutationOptions` here; it must actually be in lexical scope at this point in `createTRPCOptionsProxy` (and be the same value used by the query/infinite-query/subscription branches), otherwise this is either a compile error or silently forwards an unrelated binding.
findings.rationale: The hunk does not show where `prefix` is declared. In this factory the path/prefix are usually derived in the proxy's `createRecursiveProxy` callback, so it is plausible but not visible here. Low-to-medium confidence; worth verifying that `prefix` is the same variable the sibling `queryOptions`/`infiniteQueryOptions` builders use rather than an outer-scope shadowed value.

findings.claim: Adding `prefix` to the mutation key/options construction changes the generated mutation key shape, which can break existing callers that match mutations by key.
findings.rationale: `trpcMutationOptions` derives the `mutationKey` from `path` (and now `prefix`). Any consumer calling `queryClient.isMutating({ mutationKey })`, `getMutationCache().find(...)`, or `setMutationDefaults(...)` with a key built the old way (or by a helper that was not updated to include `prefix`) will no longer match. This is a silent runtime behavior change rather than a type error. Medium confidence — it depends on whether every other mutation-key producer in the package was updated in the same change.

findings.claim: Possible inconsistency: `prefix` is added to `mutationOptions` but the surrounding `queryOptions`/`infiniteQueryOptions`/`subscriptionOptions` branches may not have been updated identically.
findings.rationale: If only the mutation branch gains the prefix, query keys and mutation keys become namespaced differently, so utilities that strip/compare prefixes (e.g. invalidation helpers keyed off a shared root) will disagree. Low-to-medium confidence since only the mutation hunk is shown; please confirm the other option builders in this same file pass `prefix` too.
